You already have a laptop or desktop PC, but now AMD thinks you need another one—an “agent PC” to support your main machine.

AMD has responded to the growing success of OpenClaw’s AI agents with a new suggestion: customers should buy “agent PCs,” which would take the power of the Ryzen AI Max+ processor (surprise!) and repurpose it to run an agent swarm. AMD’s idea is that you should use a “normal” PC plus a secondary agent PC for running AI apps.

title: AMD wants you to buy a $2,000 ‘agent PC’ just for AI

Windows 11 finally supports displays with refresh rates of over 1,000Hz — even if such displays haven’t largely advanced past the drawing board.

On Thursday, Microsoft released Windows 11 Builds 26100.8106 and 26200.8106 to the Release Preview Channel, which include explicit support for monitors that can report refresh rates higher than 1,000Hz. Blur Busters’ Mark Rejhon took credit, and indicated that the maximum refresh rate might be as high as 5,000Hz.

title: Windows 11 paves the way for eye-melting 1,000Hz monitors

description:
Whether you’re like me and are a bit of a weather geek or you just like staring at pretty satellite images, Zoom Earth is worth checking out. This nifty site shows global weather and climate data in near real-time on an interactive map.

It’s more than just satellite images, too. There are tons of different settings and overlays you can play around with such as rain maps, wind forecast maps, temperature maps, and more. The tracking is so accurate that I began using it as my main source of weather forecasting a while back.
title: Track global weather and climate data in real time with this site
